title: Far-Right Election Groups Are Now Targeting Nursing Homes
gist: Weeks before the midterms, election denial groups led by Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network are mobilising followers to contact nursing homes over unproven voter-fraud claims, aided by a July CMS memo that replaced guidance on helping residents vote with prosecution threats. Democratic senators say the rules risk disenfranchising 2 million residents.

insights.claim: The Election Integrity Network is claiming without evidence that left-wing groups commit voter fraud in nursing homes, care homes and assisted-living facilities, and is recruiting followers to contact and question those facilities weeks before the midterms.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Expect pressure on care facilities and possible friction at polling-assistance programmes ahead of the midterms; a source of election-administration noise.
insights.locator: With just weeks to go until the midterms

insights.claim: Network founder Cleta Mitchell cites a 2020 Wisconsin case in which a sheriff alleged eight care-home residents had votes filled out for them, a claim the Wisconsin Election Commission rejected and which could not have changed the outcome since Trump lost Wisconsin by over 20,000 votes.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: The headline evidence is numerically too small to matter, so the narrative is a mobilisation tool, not an electoral fact.
insights.locator: As evidence, Mitchell referenced a case in Wisconsin

insights.claim: The network distributes a downloadable toolkit for emailing and calling local nursing homes and shared posts mapping residential care facilities in competitive districts in Arizona, California, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania and Virginia, labelling residents as potential targets for 'political predators'.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Targeting competitive districts shows the campaign is tied to House control; watch these races for related disputes.

insights.claim: New York-based Project Civicia has launched a similar 'Adopt a Care Facility' campaign, repeating the CMS Wisconsin claims, though cofounder Kim Hermance says the group does not presume wrongdoing because residents need voting assistance.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: The tactic is spreading beyond one group, suggesting a coordinated, multi-organisation front on care-facility voting.
insights.locator: Another election denial group, the New York–based Project Civicia

insights.claim: In July the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services issued a memo removing guidance on how nursing home staff could help residents vote, such as mail-in assistance or transport to polls, and replacing it with threats of prosecution for inappropriate coercion or rights violations.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Staff may stop assisting residents out of legal fear, reducing turnout among nursing home residents; a policy change to monitor for litigation.
insights.locator: In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

insights.claim: The examples cited in the CMS memo did not lead to any proven cases of voter fraud, even though the memo said the agency had become aware of several allegations of unlawfully violated resident rights.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: The policy rests on allegations rather than proven fraud, which strengthens the legal case for challenges to the memo.

insights.claim: Senators led by Elizabeth Warren and Alex Padilla wrote in August that the CMS changes would disenfranchise the country's roughly 2 million nursing home residents rather than protect them, accusing CMS of trying to intimidate staff.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Democratic oversight pressure on CMS under administrator Mehmet Oz is likely to continue and could escalate post-midterms.
insights.quote: CMS issued a memo that appears to be an attempt to intimidate nursing home staff from assisting residents in the voting process
insights.locator: In August, senators led by Elizabeth Warren and Alex Padilla

insights.claim: The Election Integrity Network has close ties to the White House, and its nursing home claims join noncitizen voting and mail-in fraud narratives that the Trump administration has supercharged as part of a broader push to undermine trust in the midterms.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Official amplification raises the odds of post-election challenges; a source of political and institutional risk around the midterms.
